summary: the potential constant, the rest position and the well's energy of a harmonic well fitted by least squares to energies at positions about a minimum

inputs.name: points
inputs.meaning: the energy curve: pairs of a position along one coordinate (a bond length, a displacement) and the energy computed or measured there, each part in one unit throughout, three distinct positions or more

outputs.name: force_constant
outputs.meaning: k of U = U0 + k (x - x0)^2 / 2: twice the fitted curvature, in the unit of the energies over the square of the unit of the positions; null when not fitted

outputs.name: rest_position
outputs.meaning: x0, the position of the fitted minimum, in the unit of the positions; null when the curvature is not positive

outputs.name: well_energy
outputs.meaning: U0, the fitted energy at x0, in the unit of the energies

outputs.name: residual_standard_deviation
outputs.meaning: the residual sum of squares over n - 3, rooted, in the unit of the energies; null with three points, where no degree of freedom is left

outputs.name: minimum_inside_span
outputs.meaning: true where x0 lies between the smallest and the largest position of the points; a minimum outside them is an extrapolation

outputs.name: why
outputs.meaning: why nothing was fitted, or why there is no minimum; absent when fitted

validity: a well that is harmonic over the positions handed: the anharmonic terms of a real bond bend the fitted k and x0 as the span widens, and this skill does not say by how much; a span that does not hold the minimum gives an extrapolated x0, which minimum_inside_span marks

source.citation: HOOMD-blue 7.2.2 documentation, hoomd.md.bond.Harmonic (read 2026-11-21, https://hoomd-blue.readthedocs.io/en/latest/hoomd/md/bond/harmonic.html; mat-20261120-hoomd-7.2.2-bond-harmonic), for the model; NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Section 4.4.3.1 Least Squares (read 2026-11-17, https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmd/section4/pmd431.htm; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261117-nist-sematech-least-squares), for the fit
source.locus: Harmonic: U(r) = 1/2 k (r - r0)^2, k the potential constant in energy per length squared and r0 the rest length; Section 4.4.3.1: least squares chooses the parameters that minimise the sum of squared deviations, and the residual standard deviation is that sum over n - p, rooted

note: Written for meta_agent/tasks/031, where a Quantum ESPRESSO agent fits the H2 bond to pw.x total energies and hands k and r0 to a HOOMD-blue agent; the relation names the well, not the molecule, and its cases are worked on two unrelated kinds of system. No value of either source stands behind the worked cases: each is an exact parabola worked by hand in its worked field, so the fit must return the parabola's own k, x0 and U0.
